Postigo''', officially the '''Municipality of Leon B. Postigo''' ({{langx|ceb|Lungsod sa Leon B. Postigo}}; [[Subanon language|Subanen]]: ''Benwa Leon B. Postigo''; [[Chavacano]]: ''Municipalidad de Leon B. Postigo''; {{langx|tl|Bayan ng Leon B. Postigo}}), is a [[municipality of the Philippines|municipality]] in the [[Philippine Province|province]] of [[Zamboanga del Norte]], [[Philippines]]. According to the 2024 census, it has a population of 29,535 people.{{PH wikidata|population_reference}} ==History== In the early 1980s, the councils of six ''[[barangay]]s'', along with residents of Maras, in the then southern [[Sindangan]] demanded for a new municipality, which was originally proposed to be called ''Talinga'', with the barangay with the same name, located 11 kilometers from [[Poblacion]], to be the seat of government. The proposed municipality was to intervene the distance of Sindangan and [[Salug]] from each other, which were about 40 kilometers.{{cite book |date=1982 |title=Record of the Batasan: Proceedings and debates, Fourth regular session, 1981–1982; volume five |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=frEjAQAAMAAJ |location=[[Philippines]] |publisher=[[Batasang Pambansa (legislature)|Batasang Pambansa]] |pages=2786–2794 |access-date=March 6, 2024 |via=[[Google Books]]}} [[Batasang Pambansa (legislature)|Then assemblyman]] Guardson R. Lood sponsored ''Parliamentary Bill No. 300'', which was also co-authored by eight other assemblymen. The bill was approved as ''[[Batas Pambansa]] Blg. 204'' on March 25, 1982; 17 ''barangays'' in southwestern part of the mother municipality, but excluding Maras, were separated to create the municipality, originally named '''Bacungan''', with another barangay with the same name, which was not included in the original plan, to be the seat of government.{{cite web |url=http://www.chanrobles.com/bataspambansa/bataspambansablg204.html |title=Batas Pambansa Blg. 204 |date=March 25, 1982 |website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |publisher=Chan Robles & Associates Law Firm |access-date=}} A plebiscite for ratification, along with ten more newly-created [[local government in the Philippines|local entities]] including nearby [[Godod]], was held on May 17, coinciding with [[1982 Philippine barangay elections|the barangay elections]].{{cite web |url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1982/07/26/official-month-in-review-may-1982/ |title=Official Month in Review: May 1982 |date=July 26, 1982 |website=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |publisher=[[Government of the Philippines]] |access-date=March 6, 2024}} * {{cite web |url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1982/04/29/proclamation-no-2188-s-1982/ |title=Proclamation No. 2188, s. 1982 |date=April 29, 1982 |website=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |publisher=[[Government of the Philippines]] |access-date=March 6, 2024}} It was renamed to its current name by virtue of ''[[Republic Act]] No. 6830'' on December 30, 1989,{{cite web |url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno6830.html |title=Republic Act No. 6830 |date=December 30, 1989 |website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |publisher=Chan Robles & Associates Law Firm |access-date=}} in honor of Leon Bayot Postigo, a [[Philippine Constabulary]] corporal whose 10-hectare lot in the town was donated by his heirs to the local government.{{cite web |url=http://leonbpostigo.gov.ph/creation-of-leon-b-postigo/ |title=Creation of Leon B. Postigo as a Municipality |accessdate=2012-04-15 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130726040102/http://leonbpostigo.gov.ph/creation-of-leon-b-postigo/ |archivedate=2013-07-26 }} ==Geography== ===Barangays=== Leon B. Postigo is politically subdivided into 18 [[barangay]]s.
